question: Every cell has a _________ around it to keep its own contents separate from the external environment.
solution:
The correct answer is __**membrane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The cell membrane, also known as the plasma membrane, is a biological membrane that separates and protects the interior of all cells from the outside environment.
 
• The membrane is selectively permeable, allowing certain substances to pass through while blocking others, maintaining the cell's internal environment.
 
• It is composed primarily of a lipid bilayer, with embedded proteins that perform various functions such as transport, signaling, and structural support.
 
• The fluid mosaic model describes the cell membrane as a dynamic structure with lipids and proteins moving laterally within the layer, providing flexibility and functionality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lipid Bilayer**

 
 
• The lipid bilayer forms the basic structure of the cell membrane, with hydrophobic tails facing inward and hydrophilic heads facing outward, creating a barrier to most water-soluble substances.
 
• It provides fluidity and flexibility to the membrane, allowing for cell movement and growth.
 
 
 
• **Membrane Proteins**
 
 
• Membrane proteins are integral or peripheral proteins that assist in various functions such as transporting molecules, acting as enzymes, or serving as receptors.
 
• These proteins are crucial for communication between the cell and its environment.
 
 
 
• **Selective Permeability**
 
 
• The selective permeability of the cell membrane allows the cell to maintain homeostasis by regulating the entry and exit of substances.
 
• It ensures that essential molecules such as nutrients and ions can enter the cell while waste products are removed.
 
 
 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model**
 
 
• Proposed by S.J. Singer and G.L. Nicolson in 1972, this model describes the cell membrane as a fluid, dynamic structure with proteins embedded in or attached to a fluid lipid bilayer.
 
• The model emphasizes the flexibility and varied functions of the membrane components.
